profile.name: Shamaryah Udeakpu
profile.title: Embedded Systems · Robotics · Hardware Engineer
profile.bio: I'm a mechatronics engineering student at FUTO who thinks in systems and builds in the real world. From embedded microcontrollers to full mechanical assemblies — I tackle problems others walk past. GDG Embedded Systems and Robotics Lead and RAIN community lead at FUTO, CODET 1st place winner, and a lifelong builder looking for engineering internships.

projects.title: SunrootLearn
projects.tagline: An AI tutor and virtual lab for every student, and a live mastery map for every teacher.
projects.problem: Students pass exams on topics they never really understood, and teachers only find out after the exam. Most schools cannot afford labs, so hands-on STEM stays out of reach.
projects.solution: A teacher uploads a syllabus and the AI drafts the topic map, lessons, two-voice podcasts in eight languages, simulations and quizzes. The teacher approves what students see. Learners study, run virtual labs and play quests, and a Bayesian Knowledge Tracing model keeps a per-topic 'cognitive twin' of what each student really knows.
projects.result: A live web app and Android app with a class mastery heatmap, six quest task types, a circuit bench and 3D robotics, and more than 3,900 automated tests run on every change. The next step is a classroom pilot to measure real learning gains.
projects.description: Built by Shamaryah as founder. It grew out of two earlier builds, CogniTwin AI and the SunRoot study lab, and now runs as one platform for teachers and learners. The pitch is honest about what is not proven yet: learning gains in a real class.
highlights: Teacher stays in control: nothing reaches students until it is approved and pushed
Per-topic mastery heatmap instead of a single exam score
Maker Studio: circuits, 3D, block coding and C++
Native Android app with in-app updates

projects.title: EcoVital
projects.tagline: Air monitoring that speaks: your air, explained out loud, with advice you can act on.
projects.problem: Dust, stale air and dry or humid rooms hurt classrooms, offices and homes, but nobody notices until people feel unwell. Typical monitors show numbers that mean little to most people.
projects.solution: A small ESP32 pod reads dust, air quality, temperature and humidity, shows them on a round dial and says what is wrong and what to do, in English, Naija Pidgin, Igbo, Yoruba or Hausa. A web app and Android app handle pairing, live dashboards, short-term forecasts, an Ask EcoVital assistant, emergency alerts and over-the-air firmware updates.
projects.result: A working pod and cloud platform. Its first public showing was the AI Builders Pitch Party at FUTO on 4 November 2026. Readings are labelled Measured or Estimated and shown as relative indexes, never as lab units.
projects.description: Each pod enrolls itself with a private token, pairs to an account with a six-character code, and keeps working through quiet hours and Wi-Fi drops. Forecasts come from a small ridge regression per reading that is only used when it beats a no-change guess.
highlights: Spoken advice in five languages
Early-warning forecasts at +10, +30 and +60 minutes
Emergency siren and one-tap 112 calling on Android
Honest by design: no medical claims, no fake units

projects.title: Scout Screener
projects.tagline: Rank candidates against a role and see the evidence from each CV. The AI suggests. A human decides.
projects.problem: Recruiters at early-stage startups read hundreds of CVs and rank them by gut feeling, so good candidates are missed. AI screeners often hide why someone scored well, and can quietly reject people.
projects.solution: Scout scores every CV against the role requirements and quotes the exact line that backs each one. 'Not stated in the CV' means verify, never reject. Employers get a job pipeline, a candidate drawer and an Ask Scout assistant. Candidates upload a CV once, see where they would rank and apply to roles they choose.
projects.result: A working hiring platform with ranked candidate lists, evidence tables, short apply links, optional accounts and a three-question candidate chat. Contact details stay private until the candidate agrees, and records expire automatically.
projects.description: Built around the principle that the AI never makes a hire or reject decision. It works without an AI key using keyword matching, and with a Groq key it adds AI screening, interview chat and CV photo reading.
highlights: Every score is backed by a quote from the CV
Privacy first: consent-based contact details, 30-day expiry
Kanban pipeline per job with drag to move stages
Works in demo mode with no setup

projects.title: AutoDiag-Point
projects.tagline: A phone-powered reader for malaria rapid tests, built for clinics with no lab and no internet.
projects.problem: Most malaria rapid tests in rural Nigeria are read by eye, once, and never recorded. Many real positive lines are only 2 to 10% as dark as the control line, which is easy to miss.
projects.solution: Cassettes sit in a light-tight tray or rotary disk under a phone camera. An ESP32 turns each slot into place over Bluetooth and sets the LED ring brightness. The phone crops each cassette, finds the control line, measures the Pf line across five photos and returns positive, faint positive, negative, uncertain or invalid, with plain advice.
projects.result: A working prototype. On the bench on 7 November 2026 it read five cassettes in one tray and agreed with the human reading on all five. A kiosk version with a waste chute and sharps container is modelled in 3D. Built for the USPF Changemaker Challenge 2026.
projects.description: The result photos in the gallery are real strips from that bench run. The reader keeps the photos of every result as a record for follow-up and works fully offline.
highlights: 7 cassettes per batch, 5 photos each
Rotary-disk kiosk concept with ArUco markers, status LEDs and biohazard bin
Photo record of every result for follow-up
Works offline

projects.title: Depth by Ear
projects.tagline: A wearable that turns the shape of a room into sound a blind user can place by ear.
projects.problem: Blindness in Nigeria is large and growing, and about 84% of it is avoidable, yet imported assistive devices price most people out. Existing wearables mostly give haptic buzzes, not a sense of where things are.
projects.solution: Time-of-flight and ultrasonic sensors on a two-servo pan/tilt gimbal scan the room. A phone fuses the range data with its camera to tell people from furniture, points the gimbal at what matters over Bluetooth, and plays the result as binaural 3D sound with a cap of 3 to 5 voices so silence stays the default.
projects.result: A full research brief, a link budget that fits a throttled 20 Hz Bluetooth stream, a costed Nigeria build, and two working browser simulators: one for the gimbal sweep and pointing logic, one for hearing the sound mapping. Hardware is the next phase.
projects.description: The simulator on the cover is the gimbal state machine running a sample scan: the wide wedge is the camera view, the bright wedge is the sensor beam, and objects appear as they are sensed.
highlights: Closed loop: camera points the sensor, sensor reports angle and distance
Costed for Nigeria: about N103,000 to N140,000 retail with a bulk-import path to close the gap
Designed for unreliable power and mid-range Android phones
Web Audio HRTF prototype to test the sound design before any hardware

projects.title: SARYX Robot Dashboard
projects.tagline: A web control room that drives a robot through its phone, with live video, map and telemetry.
projects.problem: Driving a robot remotely normally needs custom radios and a lot of hardware, which makes small robots hard to build, test and demo.
projects.solution: The robot's brain is a phone. It streams live video over WebRTC and publishes position and sensor data. The dashboard shows the stream, a live map, wheel encoder ticks, ultrasonic distance and bump status, and sends manual and training commands, waypoint recording and a remote lock command, all through Firebase.
projects.result: A deployable Next.js dashboard with a defined Firebase data model for telemetry, position, commands and WebRTC signaling, ready to pair with the robot phone app.
highlights: WebRTC video with Firestore signaling
Realtime Database for commands and telemetry
Manual and training drive modes with waypoint recording
Ships to Vercel with environment-based config

projects.title: ClassAir
projects.tagline: A classroom air purifier with a water-mist stage, built to be tested, not assumed.
projects.problem: Chalk dust and stale air build up in crowded classrooms, and commercial purifiers cost too much for most schools.
projects.solution: Room air passes a dust sensor, rises through an ultrasonic water mist and a droplet mesh, then foam, carbon and HEPA-type media before a 12 V fan pushes it out. An ESP32 smooths the dust reading, sets fan speed in three steps and switches the mist off above 60% humidity.
projects.result: A Phase 1 bench unit fully designed in a 3D assembly model with an explode slider, part-by-part fitting notes, wiring and build steps. A chalk-dust test with the unit off, fan only and fan plus mist decides whether the mist stays.
projects.description: Dust readings use a median of 15 samples plus a moving average. The mist stage adds roughly N12,000 to the earlier N41,500 estimate and is treated as an experiment.
highlights: Three-step fan curve: 30 / 60 / 100%
Humidity guard against mould
Droplet mesh keeps filters dry
Scale check: bench proof first, box-fan version for full classrooms

projects.title: Glucose Wearable Sensor Stack
projects.tagline: A nine-part wrist module for glucose-trend and cardiovascular screening research.
projects.problem: Fingerprick glucose checks are painful and give only occasional readings. No non-invasive sensor has been validated to replace a glucometer, so any attempt needs honest ground truth.
projects.solution: An ESP32-S3 wrist module combines short-wave infrared, bioimpedance, PPG and ECG, spectral skin tone, skin temperature, motion and ambient climate sensors. Each has one job, and a phone model learns from all of them against paired fingerprick or CGM readings.
projects.result: A 3D walkthrough of the module with a measurement cycle you can step through, an interactive sensor explorer with live traces, an I2C address map, the features the model sees, and a three-phase build order with go or no-go gates. It is a research prototype, not a medical device.
highlights: Found and fixed an I2C address collision
Phases prove the signal before a custom PCB
Ethics approval and NAFDAC rules called out up front

projects.title: Fingertip Air Mouse
projects.tagline: A finger-worn air mouse: tilt to move, pinch to click.
projects.problem: Pointing devices need a desk or big arm gestures, and presenters and people on the move have no small, comfortable alternative.
projects.solution: An MPU6050 motion sensor and a TTP223 touch pad sit on the fingertip so hand motion moves the cursor and a thumb pinch clicks. Six thin wires run to an ESP32-C3 Mini on the back of the hand, powered by a small LiPo through a TP4056, with an optional vibration motor for click feedback.
projects.result: A complete build package: a colour-coded wiring diagram with a tick-off wire list, a to-scale placement guide for the hand, axis orientation and pre-power-on checks.
highlights: Data-ready interrupt with a timer fallback
Pinch-to-click, no moving parts
Rechargeable 100 to 200 mAh LiPo

projects.title: Patient History Dashboard
projects.tagline: Day, week and month charts of a patient monitor’s logged readings.
projects.problem: A bedside monitor shows the current number, but nobody can see how a patient's readings changed over hours or days.
projects.solution: A web dashboard that reads logged readings from Google Sheets and charts them, with day (hourly average), week, month and all-time views and date pickers.
projects.result: A working history dashboard built with Chart.js that turns a spreadsheet log into trend charts.
highlights: Hourly and daily averaging
Day, week, month and all-time views

projects.title: OLED 128x64 Chunk Simulator
projects.tagline: Test your ESP32 text paging logic in the browser before wiring a display.
projects.problem: Debugging how text wraps and pages on a small OLED means flashing hardware again and again.
projects.solution: Type the message an ESP32 will show and it is split into screen-sized pages exactly as an SSD1306 128 by 64 display would render it, at size 1 (21 by 8) or size 2 (10 by 4).
projects.result: A working simulator with word wrap, hard breaks, long-word splitting, page controls and a tap-to-jump chunk list.
highlights: Matches the real 6x8 and 12x16 character grids
Tap-to-jump page list

projects.title: Nigeria Problem-Solution Map
projects.tagline: 45 startup ideas matched to real problems in Nigeria.
projects.problem: Founders often pick an idea first and look for a problem second.
projects.solution: A map that pairs forty-five startup ideas with concrete problems people face in Nigeria.
projects.result: A reference map used to decide which problems are worth building for.
highlights: 45 ideas mapped to specific local problems

projects.title: PET Filament Recycling Machine
projects.tagline: Turning plastic waste into 3D-printer filament — the award-winning CODET build.
projects.description: A machine that recycles PET plastic waste (like used bottles) into usable 3D-printer filament. Built and presented at the CODET Engineering Competition (Council of Deans of Engineering & Technology), South-East zone, where it helped secure 1st and 3rd place overall and a place at the national finals in Abuja. It tackles plastic pollution while producing a low-cost material for makers and engineers.
highlights: Led the team that presented the machine at the CODET South-East competition
Took 1st & 3rd place overall and qualified for the national finals in Abuja
Converts waste PET into 3D-printing filament — sustainability meets engineering
projects.problem: Plastic bottles pile up as waste, while 3D-printer filament stays expensive for makers.
projects.solution: A machine that melts and extrudes recycled PET into filament with controlled heating and extrusion.
projects.result: Won 1st and 3rd place overall at the CODET South-East competition and qualified for the national finals in Abuja.

projects.title: Quadruped Robot Dog
projects.tagline: A four-legged walking robot with servo-driven, gait-controlled legs.
projects.description: A four-legged walking robot built from the ground up. Each leg is servo-driven, and a custom gait controller coordinates the legs so the robot balances and walks on its own across surfaces.
highlights: Servo-driven legs with coordinated gait control
Balances across each step for stable walking
Built and programmed end-to-end with Arduino
projects.problem: Wheels struggle on rough ground and steps. Legged robots handle them but need careful leg coordination.
projects.solution: Four servo-driven legs, with a custom gait controller on Arduino that coordinates them to keep balance.
projects.result: A quadruped that balances and walks on its own across surfaces.

projects.title: Quadruped Spider
projects.tagline: A multi-leg spider walker with synchronised servo locomotion.
projects.description: A spider-style walking robot that drives many servos in synchrony to produce a smooth, insect-like crawling motion. A study in multi-limb coordination and balance.
highlights: Coordinates many servos for smooth crawling
Insect-like locomotion across surfaces
Hands-on multi-servo control
projects.problem: Multi-legged walkers are hard to coordinate smoothly.
projects.solution: Many servos driven in synchrony to produce a smooth, insect-like crawl.
projects.result: A working spider walker that crawls across surfaces.

projects.title: Self-Driving Car
projects.tagline: An autonomous car prototype that senses and steers itself.
projects.description: An autonomous car prototype that senses its surroundings and steers itself using onboard control logic — no hands on the wheel. Combines sensing, decision logic, and motor control.
highlights: Onboard sensing for autonomous navigation
Self-steering with no manual control
Sensor data handling and control logic in Python
projects.problem: A car needs a driver to go anywhere.
projects.solution: Onboard sensors, decision logic in Python and motor control let the car sense its surroundings and steer itself.
projects.result: An autonomous car prototype that drives with no hands on the wheel.

projects.title: Obstacle-Avoiding Car
projects.tagline: Ultrasonic sensing with real-time auto steer-around.
projects.description: A robot car that fires ultrasonic pulses to detect obstacles ahead, then autonomously steers around them in real time. A clean demonstration of sense-think-act robotics.
highlights: Ultrasonic obstacle detection
Real-time autonomous steer-around
Reliable sense-think-act loop
projects.problem: A moving robot must avoid crashing into things it cannot see.
projects.solution: An ultrasonic sensor pings ahead and the car steers around obstacles in real time with a sense-think-act loop.
projects.result: A car that detects obstacles and steers around them on its own.

projects.title: Smart Home System
projects.tagline: Home automation for lights, devices & security — on command.
projects.description: A home-automation system that controls lights, appliances, and security remotely through connected ESP microcontrollers. Brings everyday devices online and under control.
highlights: Remote control of lights, appliances & security
Built around connected ESP microcontrollers
Practical IoT for the home
projects.problem: Lights, appliances and door security are controlled by hand, and only when you are there.
projects.solution: Connected ESP microcontrollers put lights, devices and security online and under remote control.
projects.result: A working home-automation system for lights, appliances and security.

projects.title: Wearable Health Monitor
projects.tagline: A wearable that tracks vital signs in real time.
projects.description: A wearable device that tracks vital health signals like heart rate in real time and reports them back to the wearer — engineering meets well-being.
highlights: Real-time vital-sign tracking
Compact wearable form factor
Sensor integration with ESP
projects.problem: Vital signs such as heart rate are only checked occasionally.
projects.solution: A wearable with sensors and an ESP microcontroller tracks vital signs continuously and reports them to the wearer.
projects.result: A wearable that tracks vital signs in real time.

projects.title: Smart Door Lock
projects.tagline: ESP-based secure electronic access control.
projects.description: An electronic smart lock built around an ESP microcontroller, providing secure, controlled access to a door from a connected device.
highlights: Secure electronic access control
Connected, controllable lock
Built on ESP
projects.problem: Metal keys get lost, copied or forgotten.
projects.solution: An ESP-based electronic lock gives controlled access to a door from a connected device.
projects.result: A working smart lock providing secure, controlled access.

projects.title: AI Voice Calculator
projects.tagline: A voice-controlled calculator powered by speech AI.
projects.description: A voice-controlled calculator that recognises spoken numbers and operations using speech AI, then returns the result hands-free. A friendly intro to applied AI and voice interfaces.
highlights: Recognises spoken input via speech AI
Hands-free, voice-driven results
Applied AI with Python
projects.problem: Calculators need hands and eyes.
projects.solution: Speech AI in Python recognises spoken numbers and operations and returns the result.
projects.result: A hands-free, voice-driven calculator.
